entities.summary:
Axiothea of Phlius (b. 400 BCE, Phlius) was a prominent figure in the Classical era, a time of significant cultural, philosophical, and political transformation in the ancient Greek world.


She was a key thinker and philosopher, whose ideas and contributions have had a lasting impact on the development of Western philosophy.


Her influence can be seen in the works of later philosophers such as Plato and Aristotle, who built upon her ideas and expanded upon her concepts.


Axiothea's significance extends beyond the realm of philosophy, as she was also a prominent figure in the cultural and intellectual life of Phlius, a city-state that played an important role in the spread of Greek culture throughout the Mediterranean.


Despite the limitations of our knowledge about her life, Axiothea's legacy continues to be felt in the many ways in which her ideas and contributions have shaped the course of Western thought and culture.
